raw.title: 1. Audit transient hits versus sustained axial-roll success
raw.hypothesis: Transient axial-spin bursts inflate any-hit episode success because a pen can briefly satisfy the native predicate before losing stable in-hand rotation.

prediction.rationale: Baseline is any native-success step in an episode; the alternative requires native success throughout the final 60 steps, with early termination counted as failure. A 20-percentage-point reduction on identical trajectories would materially change expert qualification.

protocol.command: gpu run bash -lc 'source ~/IsaacLab/source_env.sh && python scripts/run_shadowhand_spin_stages.py --config config/shadowhand_spin_stages.yaml --research-protocol episode_rule_audit'
code_changes: Extend the existing smoke script and config with the declared research-protocol CLI and profile; freeze ten probe cases per stage before rollout.

Add an Isaac manifest/schema adapter under lares/envs/isaac_pen_spin: record reset provenance, named 157-d observation fields, normalized-to-environment action mapping, termination, and all 360 step predicates.
Evaluate fixed neutral-pose and open-loop digit-oscillation controllers on each case; score both episode reducers offline from the same traces, pooling stages with equal weight.
Add reducer and quaternion-axis tests that distinguish long-axis roll from end-over-end rotation; retain per-stage results and raw angular velocity.
Document the sustained rule as the preregistered qualification rule for the following studies, not as an already validated task definition; do not promote a policy in this audit.

raw.falsified_by: A paired interval entirely above a sustained-minus-any-hit difference of -0.20 rules out the predicted reduction on these diagnostic controllers; an interval containing zero is inconclusive about a directional difference.

raw.title: 2. Can feedback-controlled finger gaiting qualify a scripted expert?
raw.hypothesis: Feedback that alternates finger contacts while correcting pen-centre drift sustains axial rolling better than an open-loop finger oscillator.

prediction.rationale: Baseline is the frozen open-loop oscillator from idea 1, rerun on fresh cases. A 0.20 sustained-success gain would justify contact feedback, but qualification additionally requires at least 0.90 success on each stage's 30 promotion cases.

code_changes: Add lares/envs/isaac_pen_spin/scripted_expert.py with bounded joint-target finger gaiting, long-axis angular-velocity feedback, and pen-centre correction using audited named observation fields rather than guessed offsets.
Extend the existing script/config with scripted_expert_qualification; depend on idea 1's tested adapter and episode reducer.
Freeze controller code and constants before opening these manifests; evaluate both controllers on cases 0-9 for screening and 10-39 for promotion in each stage, with no tuning on these cases.

Use the unchanged strictly positive paired t-interval rule for any promotion claim; tied success is not improvement. Separately report whether either scripted controller qualifies as a demonstration source.
Save full observation/action traces from qualifying episodes with manifest, controller, schema, and reducer hashes; document that these demonstrate axial roll, not end-over-end twirling.
Reference the briefing's completed negative pretrained-policy search; do not repeat it or silently substitute an Allegro end-over-end policy.

raw.falsified_by: An upper paired interval bound below +0.20 rules out the predicted gain; failure to reach 0.90 sustained success means the controller does not qualify for that stage regardless of return.

raw.title: 3. Conditional PPO fallback: does reward optimization yield a usable expert?
raw.hypothesis: On-policy PPO learns state-dependent multi-finger coordination that sustains axial rolling on stages where the frozen scripted controllers cannot qualify.

prediction.rationale: Baseline is the best scripted controller selected by idea 2's screening results and rerun on fresh cases. A 0.10 sustained-success gain tests whether reward optimization helps, while expert qualification still requires at least 0.90 success rather than merely higher return.

protocol.command: gpu run bash -lc 'source ~/IsaacLab/source_env.sh && python scripts/isaac/train_pen_spin_expert.py --config config/shadowhand_spin_stages.yaml --research-protocol conditional_ppo_expert'
code_changes: Gate execution on idea 2: spend nothing if a scripted expert qualifies for every stage; evaluate PPO only for unresolved stages. The public-checkpoint route is already excluded by the briefing's search.
Add this training entrypoint because none of the inventoried scripts trains rsl_rl PPO; instantiate the vendored ShadowHandSpinPPORunnerCfg and reuse the existing stage configuration.

Predeclare an initial cap of 30000 completed training episodes per stage, with Stage1-to-Stage2-to-Stage3 weight transfer where required; count resets explicitly. This is an initial measurement budget, not a GPU ceiling.
Freeze training reset schedules before execution; use the final scheduled checkpoint, never imitation loss or promotion results, for this first qualification attempt.
Reuse the existing rollout script and idea 1's adapter for paired PPO-versus-script evaluation on 30 fresh frozen cases per unresolved stage; worst-case evaluation cost is 180 episodes.
Require at least 0.90 sustained success for demonstration qualification and a paired interval lower bound above zero for an improvement claim; report reward-success disagreement explicitly.

Export qualified expert checkpoints and demonstration traces with provenance for subsequent plateau-triggered trace repair. If qualification fails, document the failure before proposing additional training or changing rewards.

raw.falsified_by: An upper paired interval bound below +0.10 rules out the predicted gain; PPO remains unusable as an expert if sustained success is below 0.90 even when mean return rises.
